name: Bali
short_description: Rice terraces, temples, and a slower pace built around wellness and creativity.

neighborhoods.name: Ubud
neighborhoods.vibe: Art, yoga, rice terraces, quiet mornings

food_highlights: Warungs (local eateries), fresh tropical fruit, plant-based cafe culture in Ubud/Canggu.
culture_notes: Hindu temple ceremonies are frequent and visible — dress modestly at temples (sarong usually provided/rented).
nature_notes: Rice terraces, volcanoes (Mount Batur sunrise hikes), waterfalls, beaches on the south coast.
transportation_notes: Scooter or private driver are the norm; traffic in the south (Canggu/Seminyak) can be heavy.

name: Santorini
best_season: Late May–June or September (shoulder season, fewer crowds)
short_description: Whitewashed cliffside towns over the caldera — built for slow mornings and sunset views.

neighborhoods.name: Oia
neighborhoods.vibe: The iconic sunset views, quieter at night

food_highlights: Fresh seafood, Assyrtiko wine from volcanic-soil vineyards, tomato fritters (a Santorini specialty).
culture_notes: Small island — most life happens along the caldera rim; peak summer (July–Aug) is very crowded and hot.
nature_notes: Volcanic caldera, black/red sand beaches, boat trips to the volcano and hot springs.
transportation_notes: Rent an ATV/car or use buses between towns; the island is walkable within each town.

name: Kyoto
best_season: Late March–early April (cherry blossoms) or November (autumn foliage)
short_description: Temples, gardens, and centuries of craft — a city built for slowing down and paying attention.

neighborhoods.name: Gion
neighborhoods.vibe: Historic geisha district, traditional wooden machiya houses

neighborhoods.name: Arashiyama
neighborhoods.vibe: Bamboo grove, river, quieter western edge of the city

neighborhoods.name: Higashiyama
neighborhoods.vibe: Temple-lined stone streets, classic postcard Kyoto

food_highlights: Kaiseki (multi-course traditional dining), matcha sweets, Nishiki Market for street food.
culture_notes: Many temples and shrines — modest dress appreciated; some areas restrict photography of geisha for privacy.
nature_notes: Bamboo groves, Zen gardens, mountain hikes (Fushimi Inari's thousand torii gates).
transportation_notes: Excellent bus and rail network; a bicycle is a great way to see the city center.

name: Tulum
short_description: Jungle meets coastline — cenotes, beach clubs, and a design-forward wellness scene.

neighborhoods.name: Tulum Pueblo (town)
neighborhoods.vibe: More local, better value, restaurant scene

food_highlights: Fresh ceviche, tropical smoothie bowls, upscale beach-club dining.
culture_notes: Near several Mayan ruins (Tulum's own clifftop ruins, plus Coba nearby).
nature_notes: Cenotes (freshwater sinkholes) for swimming/snorkeling, mangroves, reef snorkeling.
transportation_notes: Bike or scooter along the hotel zone road; a car/taxi is useful for cenotes further out.

name: Paris
short_description: Museums, cafes, and a city built around beauty in the everyday.

neighborhoods.name: Montmartre
neighborhoods.vibe: Artists' quarter, views over the city

food_highlights: Boulangeries, wine bars, market culture (Marché des Enfants Rouges).
culture_notes: The Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, and countless smaller galleries reward slow, unhurried visits.
nature_notes: The Seine riverbanks, Jardin du Luxembourg, Bois de Boulogne.
transportation_notes: Metro is extensive and fast; the city is also very walkable.

name: Miami
short_description: Beach energy and business energy at once — a city built for ambition and sunshine.
food_highlights: Cuban coffee and cafecito culture, Latin-fusion dining, fresh seafood.
culture_notes: Strong Latin American influence across food, music, and language.
nature_notes: Beaches, Everglades day trips, Biscayne Bay boating.
transportation_notes: A car is genuinely useful outside South Beach; rideshare is easy everywhere.

name: New York City
short_description: Endless neighborhoods, endless food, and a pace that matches big ambition.
food_highlights: Every cuisine imaginable; the city rewards seeking out neighborhood spots over tourist ones.
culture_notes: World-class museums (MoMA, the Met), Broadway, countless galleries.
nature_notes: Central Park, Hudson River Park, the High Line.
transportation_notes: Subway covers the whole city; walking is often faster than a cab in Manhattan.

name: Los Angeles
short_description: Spread-out and sun-drenched — a city that rewards knowing exactly which neighborhood you want.
food_highlights: Farmers markets, health-forward cafes, incredible taco culture across the city.
culture_notes: Entertainment industry hub — expect a mix of high glamour and total casualness side by side.
nature_notes: Griffith Park hikes, Malibu coastline, nearby desert day trips.
transportation_notes: A car is close to essential — the city is very spread out.

name: Lisbon
short_description: Hills, tiled facades, and golden light over the Tagus river — Europe's warmer, more relaxed capital.

neighborhoods.name: Alfama
neighborhoods.vibe: Oldest quarter, fado music, narrow lanes

food_highlights: Pastéis de nata, fresh grilled fish, natural wine bars.
culture_notes: Fado music (melancholic traditional singing) is a real cultural touchstone worth seeking out live.
nature_notes: Day trips to Sintra's palaces and coastline are very popular and worthwhile.
transportation_notes: Trams and funiculars handle the hills; the city center is walkable but steep.

name: Mexico City
short_description: One of the world's great food and art cities, at a fraction of the cost of Europe.

neighborhoods.name: Coyoacán
neighborhoods.vibe: Frida Kahlo's home, colorful, market culture

food_highlights: World-class tacos and street food, high-end tasting menus, mezcal bars.
culture_notes: Extraordinary museum density (Frida Kahlo Museum, Anthropology Museum, dozens more).
nature_notes: Chapultepec Park, day trips to Teotihuacán pyramids.
transportation_notes: Rideshare is affordable and common; the metro is extensive but can be very crowded.

name: Barcelona
short_description: Gaudí's architecture, beach access, and late-night tapas culture in one walkable city.
food_highlights: Tapas culture, fresh seafood, La Boqueria market.
culture_notes: Gaudí's Sagrada Família and Park Güell are worth booking well ahead.
nature_notes: City beaches, Montjuïc hill and gardens, Collserola natural park nearby.
transportation_notes: Metro is efficient; the city is also very bike- and walk-friendly.

name: Rome
short_description: Ancient history layered under everyday life — ruins beside espresso bars.
food_highlights: Cacio e pepe, Roman-Jewish cuisine in the Ghetto, espresso standing at the bar.
culture_notes: The Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Vatican Museums reward booking tickets in advance.
nature_notes: Villa Borghese gardens; day trips to Tivoli's gardens and villas.
transportation_notes: Historic center is very walkable; cobblestones make wheeled luggage tricky.

name: Reykjavík & the Ring Road
short_description: Waterfalls, glaciers, and geothermal springs — nature at a scale that resets your sense of self.

neighborhoods.name: Reykjavík
neighborhoods.vibe: Small, walkable capital, design shops, cafes

food_highlights: Fresh seafood, geothermal-baked bread, skyr (Icelandic yogurt).
culture_notes: Small population, English widely spoken, strong design and literary culture.
nature_notes: The core draw — waterfalls, glaciers, geothermal springs (Blue Lagoon and quieter alternatives), volcanic landscapes.
transportation_notes: Renting a car for the Ring Road is the standard way to see the country beyond Reykjavík.

name: Cape Town
short_description: Mountain, ocean, and wine country all within an hour of each other.
food_highlights: World-class wine country day trips (Stellenbosch, Franschhoek), fresh seafood.
culture_notes: Layered history — the Bo-Kaap neighborhood and Robben Island are meaningful, sobering visits.
nature_notes: Table Mountain, Cape of Good Hope, penguin colonies at Boulders Beach.
transportation_notes: A car is very useful for the Peninsula and Winelands; rideshare works well in the city.

name: Bangkok
best_for: A gateway to the rest of Thailand
short_description: Ornate temples beside night markets — one of the world's great street-food cities.
food_highlights: Street food is genuinely some of the best in the world — night markets, khao san road food stalls.
culture_notes: Buddhist temples throughout — modest dress required at the Grand Palace and major temples.
nature_notes: Chao Phraya river life; a common jumping-off point for islands and northern Thailand.
transportation_notes: BTS Skytrain avoids traffic; tuk-tuks and rideshare (Grab) are both common.

name: Copenhagen
short_description: Design, calm, and hygge — a city built around ease rather than hustle.
food_highlights: New Nordic cuisine, excellent bakeries, a strong natural wine bar scene.
culture_notes: Design museums and architecture are a real draw; the city is built around Danish design principles.
nature_notes: Harbor swimming spots in summer, extensive bike paths, nearby coastline.
transportation_notes: Biking is the primary way locals get around — very bike-friendly infrastructure.

name: Marrakech
short_description: Souks, riads, and hammams — an intensely visual, textured city.
food_highlights: Tagines, mint tea culture, Jemaa el-Fnaa night market food stalls.
culture_notes: Bargaining is customary in the souks; modest dress is respectful, especially away from riads/hotels.
nature_notes: Atlas Mountains day trips, desert excursions further afield.
transportation_notes: The medina is walking-only (no cars); use taxis to move between the medina and modern districts.

name: London
short_description: History, world-class museums (many free), and endless distinct neighborhoods.
food_highlights: Borough Market, an extraordinary range of global cuisine, classic pub culture.
culture_notes: Many major museums (British Museum, Tate Modern) are free to enter.
nature_notes: Hyde Park, Hampstead Heath, the Thames path.
transportation_notes: The Underground (Tube) covers the whole city efficiently.

name: Tokyo
short_description: Endless neighborhoods, each with its own identity — from ancient shrines to neon streets.
food_highlights: Ramen shops, izakayas, depachika (department store food halls), sushi at every price point.
culture_notes: Extremely orderly and clean; queuing and quiet public transit etiquette are the norm.
nature_notes: Meiji Shrine's forest, Shinjuku Gyoen gardens, day trips to Mount Fuji/Hakone.
transportation_notes: The train/subway system is extensive, punctual, and the primary way to get around.

name: Costa Rica (Nosara / Guanacaste)
short_description: Jungle meets coastline — built around 'pura vida' and a real wellness culture, not just marketing.
food_highlights: Fresh tropical produce, casados (traditional plate meals), strong farm-to-table culture.
culture_notes: "Pura vida" (pure life) is a genuine cultural philosophy, not just a slogan.
nature_notes: Rainforest, cloud forest, wildlife (sloths, monkeys), surf breaks, waterfalls.
transportation_notes: A 4WD rental is often necessary — many roads are unpaved, especially in rainy season.
